Subject Alleged seizure of pistols in the house of Sz Foh Ling near Chung
San Bridge by the Zau Ka Doo Police.

Made by ............ and ............ Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang.

There are no Policeman bearing the name of Yang
Ching Ziang (楊金祥) attached to stations in the Zau Ka Doo
Division. This information was referred to Chief Inspector
Sih, who, after making further enquiries, reported that,
according to his informer, this Policeman (a Sergeant) was
transferred on the morning of February 20 (the day of the
attack on Zau Ka Doo Station) to the Chinese Police Training
Depot on Lunghua Road.

Enquiries were accordingly made at this institution
and it appears from the file kept at Headquarters that this
Sergeant was transferred to the Training Depot on February 19,
one day previous to the trouble.

An investigation was conducted by Mr. Hweng Hwa
and statements by this Police Sergeant and two other Policemen
of the Chung San Road Sub-Station (the latter two who were on duty at the time
of the trouble) were taken at his office. It appears from
these statements that Sz Foh Ling, the Mill foreman, had only
one pistol (a licenced one) in his possession and he had never
handed it to any Policeman. Mr. Hwang Hwa does not think
further investigations are necessary.

Copies of statements with translation are attached.

主题 据称曹家渡警察在中山桥附近的 Sz Foh Ling 家中搜出手枪。

制作人 ____ 和 ____ 由谭绍良警司转呈。

曹家渡区各警局并无名为杨金祥（楊金祥）的警员。此信息已转交 Sih 总督察，经进一步查询后，他报告称，据其线人透露，该名警员（一名巡长）于2月20日上午（即袭击曹家渡警局之日）被调往龙华路的中国警察训练所。

因此向该机构进行了查询，根据总部保存的档案显示，该巡长于2月19日，即骚乱发生前一天，被调往训练所。

黄华先生对此进行了调查，并在其办公室记录了该名警察巡长以及另外两名来自中山路分驻所的警员（后两人在骚乱发生时正在执勤）的供词。根据这些供词，纱厂领班 Sz Foh Ling 仅持有一支手枪（有执照），且他从未将其交给任何警员。黄华先生认为无需进一步调查。

Statement of Lin Kwan Tin (凌光鼎), age 40, native of
Kweichow.
I am the patrol officer attached to the Chow
Ka Jao (周家桥) Sub-Station. I was transferred to this
Station on the 1st instant. I have been in the Bureau
less than three months. Formerly, I was in the Peace
Preservation Corps. At 5.20 a.m. February 30, workers
surrounded the house of Sse and took Sse Foh Ling, Shih
Ching Chung and two others to Chung San Bridge. As there
was a big crowd, I sent policemen to give protection..
I ordered the crowd to elect representatives to have a
talk in the Sub-Station. After a considerable length of
time, they detailed four representatives to the Sub-
Station. Sse had a pistol in his possession but he did
not hand it to any policeman. A confusion took place.
Later, the officer i/c of the Branch Bureau also came and
ordered the workers to disperse. The representatives
together with Sse and three others were taken by the Chief
to the Branch Bureau to discuss a settlement. From the
beginning to the end, I did not see any of the four pistols
which were said to have been handed to the policemen.

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tseliang Forwarded by W. Lancies D.S.I.

In connection with the discharge by the local Tangpu of
one named Tsu Yung-kong (朱永根) from the management of the
Shanghai Municipality Western District Foreign Cotton Mill
Workers' Foh Lee Society (上海市沪西外商纱厂职工福利会), 16 Ting Keng Li,
off Jessfield Road, O.O.L., on May 12, it has been ascertained
that Tsu has been reinstated in his former position in the
Society on the instructions of Mr. Loh Ching-dz (陆京士),
committee member of the local Tangpu. This sudden change was
the result of an appeal made by four representatives of the
workers of the Toyoda Mill on or about May 13 to Loh Ching-dz,
to whom the callers stated that should the Tangpu persist in the
dismissal of Tsu Yung-kong from the Society, all workers would
sever their connections with the Society as a protest. In
view of the workers' decidedly unfavourable attitude towards
the Tangpu's decision, Loh Ching-dz agreed to rescind the order
of Tsu's dismissal.

The reinstatement of Tsu in the Society has removed the
unrest among the workers of the Toyoda Cotton Mill.

In order to avoid possible trouble with the workers, Chen
Tseliang and a few of his associates, who were responsible for
the recent dispute, are absenting themselves from the office of
the Society for the time being.

In connection with the strike of the workers of the
Toyoda Cotton Mill and subsequent attack by the strikers upon
the Jessfield Village Branch Police Station on February 20,
1937, sixteen of the assailants who were arrested by the Chinese
Police and later handed over to the Shanghai District Court for
investigation have been officially charged by the Procurator
of the Court with causing bodily harm and interfering with the
lawful discharge of public functions. The 16 defendants were
released on bail. The last hearing of the case took place on
April 4 at the Court, Nantao, when it was remanded sine die
owing to the absence of two of the 16 defendants, and the Court
ruled that the guarantors be held responsible for producing the
two absentees in question.

Sz Tsing-tsung(施進春 ), a clerk in the employ of the
Toyoda Mill, was arrested on March 23 by the Judicial Police
attached to the Shanghai District Court for being concerned in the
attempted murder of Sung Chien-tai (孫乾泰 ) on February 19,
1937 and is still detained by the Court.

With reference to the Foh Lee Society, also known as the
Shanghai Municipality Western District Foreign Cotton Mill
Workers' Foh Lee Society ( 上海市滬西外人紗廠工人福利會 ),
it has been ascertained that Van Pang-wu ( 范邦和 ), principal
figure of the Society who was responsible for instigating the
demonstration and riot has incurred the displeasure of Chu
Hsueh-fan ( 朱學範 ) and Loh Ching-dz ( 陸京士 ), two
wellknown leaders in local circles, and in order to placate
the Chinese Police, they have dismissed Van from his director-
ship of the Society. Van, following his dismissal, attempted
to join the Chung Nyi Society but his application was refused.

Made by D.S.I. Umemoto. Forwarded by O. I. Nakamura

In connection with the attempted murder of Sung Chien Tai,
information has been obtained from the management of the Toyoda
Cotton Mills to the effect that a hearing of the case against
six persons charged at the instance of Sung Chien Tai was held
at the Nantao District Court during the afternoon of March 11.
Only three defendants, namely, Shi Foh Lin (施福林), Chao
Wei Shu (趙維恕) and Chen Chih Hsiang (陳志香) appeared
before the Court. Shi Foh Lin and Chao Wei Shu denied the
charge. Chen Chih Hsiang, who admitted that he was the man
responsible for the stabbing of Sung Chien Tai, made the
following statement:-
"On November 16, 1936, Sung Chien Tai came to my home and
asked me to engage a number of loafers as he was planning to
create a disturbance at the Toyoda Cotton Mills. As he
promised to give me a tempting reward, I accepted the offer.
He did not keep his promise, however, and treated me with
indifference. Following the organisation of the Foh Lee
Association Sung became a member of the Committee of this
Society. I repeatedly approached him with a view to securing
a position in the mill through his influence, but he refused
to pay heed to my entreaties. Being indignant over this apathy
on the part of Sung, I decided to make him pay for this so I
attacked him, purely out of personal motives, on the early
morning of February 12."

Umemoto

In connection with the recent strike of the workers
of the Toyoda Cotton Mill, further information has been
obtained from reliable Japanese sources to the effect that
following the organization of the Foh Lee Association Sung
Chien Tai (施乾泰), a committee member of the Association,
engaged about 13 loafers to make use of them to expand the
influence of the newly organized society over the workers of
various industrial concerns. The Association having succeeded
in enlisting a large number of workers, numbering 3,000 persons,
Sung Chien Tai severed his connections with the loafers as
their services were no longer required. Being dissatisfied
with the action taken by Sung, the discharged loafers
repeatedly demanded of him for their reinstatements which was
refused. It is, therefore, believed that the attempted murder
of Sung Tien Tai was perpetrated by these disgruntled loafers
as retaliation.

taking advantage of this incident, shifted blame on Shi Foh

Chien Tai. As a result of this allegation, at a meeting held

19 which was presided over by Van Pang Wu, it was proposed to
attack the three aforementioned persons. The plan was carried
out on the morning of February 20.

        The dispute was settled through the mediation of Mr. Tu
Yueh-shen (杜月笙 ) and the strikers resumed work at 6 p.m.
February 20. The situation is at present quiet.
        In the middle of November last year, the workers of the

        Following the organization of the Foh Lee Association

anxious to have the trouble settled as soon as possible, the

strike and due to his efforts the strike was called off right

for the strike, but the management attributes same to the
ambitious plot of the Foh Lee Association to expand its
influence in the mills which met with a stern opposition from
the conservative element headed by the three clerks in question.
The officials of the Foh Lee Association are all well known
members of the General Labour Union as well as the Chinese
Communist Party and their principal aim is to spread Communist
influence in labour circles.

Shortly after a number of workers approached the
Charge Room of the Jessfield Village Branch Station,
demanding the arrest of Sung Jih Tai's assailant.

Being confronted with a very hostile crowd a call
was put through to the Special Unit of the Police Bureau
at Nantao for assistance.

Before the arrival of the Special Unit the crowd
began rioting and the Station greatly damaged, whilst
Col. Tan and a Chinese Constable received minor injuries
to their head and body, they were immediately removed
to the Red Cross Hospital, Avenue Haig, where they were
discharged after receiving dressing.

On the arrival of the Special Unit, a baton charge
was ordered to clear the rioters, and as many workers still
remained on the premises of the Station causing a
disturbance, some 8 or 9 shots were fired towards the
ground, during which one of the mill workers named Tseng
Vung Loong (張文龍) age 31, native of Kiangsu, residing
in a straw hut off Robison Road was injured by a stray
bullet, causing injury to his right knee, he is at
present detained in the Red Cross Hospital.

At 6.50 a.m. 20-2-37, a telephone message was received at Bubbling Well Station from the Toyoda Cotton Mill, 800 Jessfield Road reporting that approximately 3000 workers on the day shift had failed to report for work. A party of Police immediately proceeded to the mill where it was learned that large numbers of the male workers had been picketed on the various approaches to the mill and instructed the female workers to return home pending a meeting which the male workers intended to hold at the headquarters of the "Beneficial Society for the workers of Foreign Cotton Mills", 16 Loh Sung Deng, Zau Ka Deo, in regard to the stabbing of one of the Toyoda Mill workers representative named Sung Jih Tai at about 12.30 a.m. 19-2-37 in Chapei.

1937年2月20日上午6时50分，静安寺警局接到极司菲尔路800号丰田棉纺厂的电话报告，称该厂日班约3000名工人未上班。一队警察立即前往该厂，获悉大量男工在通往该厂的各条路口设置纠察线，并指示女工回家，等待男工拟于“外商银行华员益友会”（注：此处原文为“Beneficial Society for the workers of Foreign Cotton Mills”，即“外资棉厂工人福利会”）总部举行的会议。该会议地点位于曹家渡劳神登路16号（音译），议题是关于1937年2月19日凌晨12时30分左右在闸北发生的一名丰田厂工人代表宋吉泰（音译）被刺一案。

本局派出的一队着装警察部署在“丰田”经营的两家工厂。

1937年2月20日上午7时35分，根据谭伯熙上校的电话通知，静安寺警局的警察前往上海市警察局第六分局，得知上午6时30分左右，大量男工前往该分局拘留室，要求逮捕袭击宋某的行凶者。由于人群充满敌意，当局向南市特别股发出呼叫，但在他们到达之前，人群部分破坏了警局，谭上校和一名华籍巡捕受轻伤。

特别股到达后，实施了警棍驱散，警察向地面开枪约8或9发，结果一名工厂工人右膝中弹。另有5名工厂工人在警棍驱散中受轻伤，15人被捕。

1937年2月20日下午6时，约80名罢工者恢复工作，目前局势平静。

附注：57号巡长高格斯（音译）率领一支武装搜查队，于1937年2月20日上午7时至7时30分在该区各条道路行动，并于上午7时30分至11时在丰田棉纺厂待命，无报告，无逮捕。

Summarized translation of a handbill entitled
"Letter to the entire body of workers of the
Toyoda Cotton Mill" obtained by the Municipal
Police on February 25, 1937

Dear Labourers,

The imperialists are continuing to attack the poor
and labouring masses. For the sake of our rice bowls,
we have to endure all kinds of suffering and to work
like beasts. The imperialists, however, have no sympathy
for our hard life but oppress us in every way rendering our
existence almost impossible.

The Foh Lee Society (福利会), organized by the
Kuomintang, claims to work for the welfare of the workers,
but, in reality, it extracts money from the labourers.
The officers of the society are now at loggerheads simply
because they are dissatisfied with the distribution of booty.
Sung Chien Tai (沈乾泰), labour representative, is a straight
forward man and works for the emancipation of the labourers.
He does not receive any bribes from the imperialists. For
this reason the imperialists hate him and instigated their
running dog Sz Foh Ling (施福林) to make an attempt on his
life. Such a criminal should be immediately arrested and
punished, but the running dog Col Tan Pao Shou (谭保寿)
released him. Therefore the workers became angry and attacked
the Police Station. During the disturbance Col. Tan ordered
his men to arrest 16 of the workers. These workers have been
sent to Court and are still in custody. The existence of
such a running dog of the "dwarf slaves" as Col. Tan Pao Shou
cannot be tolerated and we cannot dissolve our anger towards
him even if we eat his flesh, drink his blood, and sleep on
his skin. Let us concentrate our strength and conduct a
desperate struggle against this kind of running dog. We will
request other workers to support you for the purpose of gaining

1937年2月25日由警务处查获的题为
《致丰田棉纺厂全体工人书》的传单
摘要译文

亲爱的劳工们，

帝国主义者正在继续攻击贫困的和劳动的大众。为了我们的饭碗，我们不得不忍受各种苦难，像牲畜一样工作。然而，帝国主义者对我们的艰苦生活毫无同情，反而以各种方式压迫我们，使我们的生存几乎成为不可能。

由国民党组织的福利会声称致力于工人的福利，但实际上它从劳动者那里榨取钱财。该会的官员们现在正陷入争执，仅仅是因为他们对赃款的分配不满。工人代表沈乾泰是一个正直的人，致力于为劳动者的解放而工作。他不接受帝国主义者的任何贿赂。因此，帝国主义者恨他，并唆使其走狗施福林企图杀害他。这样的罪犯本应立即逮捕并惩处，但走狗谭保寿上校却释放了他。因此，工人们愤怒地袭击了警察局。在骚乱期间，谭上校命令其手下逮捕了16名工人。这些工人已被送交法庭，目前仍在羁押中。像谭保寿上校这样的“矮奴”（指日本人）走狗的存在是不能容忍的，即使我们吃他的肉，喝他的血，睡在他的皮上，也无法消除对他的愤怒。让我们集中力量，与这种走狗进行殊死斗争。我们将请求其他工人支持你们，以期获得

the final victory. We hope you will not fall into the
trick of the imperialists and will not surrender:
Our slogans are as follows:-
1. Strike and demonstrate against the imperialists.
2. Punish Sz Foh Ling and his instigators.
3. Expel the running dog Col. Tan Pao Shou.
4. Demand the release of the arrested workers.
5. Overthrow Japanese imperialism.
6. Overthrow all of those who betray and oppress the
workers.

Shanghai Labour Federation.
February 20, 1937.
